text:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected on shared-gpu-prod (rolling window 5m). Streaming stalls increasing. SLOs breached: p95 ~220ms -> 800ms, p99 ~1.8s -> 4.6s. Auto-escalation to oncall

devon: acked, I'm oncall. pulling up dashboards now. any customer-facing impact?

sara: customer impact: two contracts reported slow responses in our support queue (ACME + Beacon). CS says retries from their side started at ~15:42 UTC. ETA on mitigation?

kyle: looking at infra. seeing I/O wait high on gpu-pool-7 nodes. baseline iowait jumped from 2% -> 28% across hosts hosting shared-gpu pool.

maria: model-side: streaming stall traces show many partial sends with stalled chunk writes at ~200-400ms intervals. correlates w/ kernel blkio spikes in node metrics.

ben: possible noisy tenant. checking top consumers by cgroup and pod.

kyle: run: kubectl get pods -n inference -l pool=shared-gpu -o wide
```
NAME                             READY   STATUS    NODE            IP            
inference-tenant-acme-0          2/2     Running   gpu-node-7      10.10.7.21    
inference-tenant-beacon-4       2/2     Running   gpu-node-5      10.10.5.14    
noisy-collector-9               1/1     Running   gpu-node-7      10.10.7.33    
```

kyle: on gpu-node-7 top I/O: `iostat -x 1 3` shows %util at 95% for nvme0n1, avg await 120ms. nvidia-smi looks normal (GPU util low). pointing to disk/block IO bottleneck from a pod hitting fs heavily (checkpointing /logs + prefix cache writes).

ben: found pid for noisy-collector on node7. its blkio cgroup shows large writes. `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/inference.slice/noisy-collector/blkio.throttle.io_service_bytes` -> many MB/s to sda.

maria: streaming stalls align with these spikes; the runtime waits for KV cache writes occasionally because we persist prefix cache to disk for that tenant (legacy behavior).

devon: immediate mitigation options?

kyle: 1) throttle blkio for noisy-collector via cgroup (quick but not ideal)
2) cordon + evict noisy pod to another node/pool (causes brief disruption but removes contention)
3) move ACME/Beacon customers to reserved pool as emergency fallback (config-level, route policy change)

sara: prioritize customer-facing: move ACME + Beacon to reserved pool if low friction. any downtime expected?

maria: we can change routing policy for those tenants to use reserved-gpu-pool-1 with fast warmup. no model change needed; should be transparent to customers. expected ~10s route propagation for new connections; existing streaming sessions will still experience stalls until reconnect.

devon: do it. kyle, can you stage a quick blkio throttle on noisy-collector as temporary while we move tenants?

kyle: applying throttle: ssh gpu-node-7 -> sudo systemd-run --scope -p BlockIOWeight=10 --slice=inference.slice /bin/bash -c 'echo 2048 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/inference.slice/noisy-collector/blkio.weight'
deploy-bot: runbook action: applied blkio weight change on gpu-node-7 by kyle at 15:45:12 UTC, run id dpl-20230315-01

kyle: throttle in place. observing nvme %util drop from 95% -> 45% over 30s. iostat await down to ~25ms.

maria: streaming stalls reduced immediately in traces. p95 dropped from ~800ms -> 260ms, p99 now ~1.1s. still above objective but much better.

devon: start tenant routing switch. ben, coordinate config change with deploy-bot. we'll move ACME then Beacon.

ben: running CLI to update route: `rwctl routes update --tenant acme --pool reserved-gpu-pool-1 --strategy immediate`

deploy-bot: route change queued for tenant=acme by ben. preview: zero-downtime for new sessions, existing sessions unaffected.

ben: ACME routed. verifying sessions: new sessions now land on reserved pool. metrics show ACME tail latency p99 down to 220ms within 2m.

sara: notifying CS and customers: "We routed your traffic to an isolated pool to mitigate observed latency; engineering is investigating root cause and will follow up." --- sent to ACME. they acknowledged. :thumbsup:

kyle: moving Beacon next. applying same route update.

maria: after Beacon move, cluster-level p95 ~180ms, p99 ~420ms. Streaming stalls back to baseline.

devon: good. we'll keep throttle in place for 30m while we do deeper postmortem. who owns the noisy collector?

ben: noisy-collector belongs to analytics team (svc-analytics). opened ticket ENGOPS-4923, tagging analytics lead. requested limit on fs writes and switch to in-memory buffering.

kyle: notes for postmortem: root cause = tenant-specific prefix-cache persistence + a non-throttled analytics pod doing heavy syncs on same NVMe, leading to blkio saturation; failure mode = streaming stalls due to runtime blocking on disk I/O for KV persistence.

maria: action items: 1) disable prefix persistence by default for shared pool tenants (flag) 2) enforce blkio weight policy for inference.slice (admit control) 3) add alert for nvme %util > 80% on shared-pool nodes 4) automated routing fallback when p99 > X for 3m

devon: i'm logging actions in the incident doc. handing off to kyle for the next 2 hours while i finish other paging. kyle, take ownership.

kyle: taking over. I'll keep throttle for 30m, follow up with analytics team, and start a postmortem draft. updating incident status -> mitigation in place, customer impact reduced.

sara: CS follow-up plan: send incident summary + mitigation + ETA on permanent fix (48-72h). labelled severity=P2 for now.

ben: bumped retention on debug traces for affected tenants to 24h. saved relevant traces and logs under ENGOPS-4923.

devon: thanks team. will check back in 2h for status. :heart:

incident-bot: NOTE: Incident run duration so far 00:25:50. Please update runbook and incident trackers.

kyle: adding final note: recommend adding a preflight check during onboarding that flags any pod that writes >20MB/s to local NVMe for shared pools.

maria: +1. also recommend evaluating moving prefix cache writes to tmpfs as optional config for low-latency tenants.

sara: will include those recommendations in the customer postmortem.

ben: linking dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.net/d/inference/shared-gpu-latency?orgId=1&from=now-30m&to=now

devon: closing slack thread for now, will re-open if regressions.
